# `react/component-max-lines`

**A React component stays under a maximum number of lines**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-react` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-react` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JSX, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:react/size` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `max`, `skip_blank_lines`, `skip_comments`, `ignore_names` |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (splitting a component means choosing which part becomes its own component and which props it takes; that is the author's call) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `@eslint-react/no-large-components` |

## What it checks

A React component spans at most `max` lines (200 by default), from its first line to its last. A component is a function whose name starts with a capital letter and that holds JSX — a declaration, an arrow or a function expression, also inside `memo(…)` or `forwardRef(…)` — or a class that extends `Component` or `PureComponent`. Blank lines and comment-only lines are not counted unless `skip_blank_lines` or `skip_comments` is `false`. `js/max-lines-per-function` measures every function; this rule measures components only, so its limit can be looser (a component is mostly markup). The rule reports on the component's name: `Component Table is 245 lines (max 200)`.

**Why:** A component that long renders several things, and a change to one of them re-reads all of them. Split out the parts that have a name of their own.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-react
pip install codelaw-rules-react
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:react/size` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:react/size"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"react/component-max-lines" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max` | `integer` | `200` | the most lines one component may span |
| `skip_blank_lines` | `boolean` | `true` | blank lines do not count |
| `skip_comments` | `boolean` | `true` | lines that hold only a comment do not count |
| `ignore_names` | `string` | *none* | a regular expression; components named like this are exempt |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."react/component-max-lines"]
severity = "error"

[rules."react/component-max-lines".options]
max = 200
skip_blank_lines = true
skip_comments = true
# ignore_names = …   # no default: unset
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"react/component-max-lines" = { severity = "error", options = { max = 3, skip_blank_lines = false, skip_comments = false, ignore_names = "^Card" } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `max`

*integer* · default `200`

the most lines one component may span

```toml
[rules."react/component-max-lines".options]
max = 3
```

#### `skip_blank_lines`

*boolean* · default `true`

blank lines do not count

```toml
[rules."react/component-max-lines".options]
skip_blank_lines = false
```

#### `skip_comments`

*boolean* · default `true`

lines that hold only a comment do not count

```toml
[rules."react/component-max-lines".options]
skip_comments = false
```

#### `ignore_names`

*string* · no default

a regular expression; components named like this are exempt

```toml
[rules."react/component-max-lines".options]
ignore_names = "^Card"
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/react/rules/react/component-max-lines.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### a component over the limit is reported on its name

```toml
[rules."react/component-max-lines".options]
max = 3
```

```jsx
function Card() {
  const a = 1;
  const b = 2;
  return <div>{a}{b}</div>;
}
```

**Reports** at `1:10`.

#### at the limit is fine

```toml
[rules."react/component-max-lines".options]
max = 5
```

```jsx
function Card() {
  const a = 1;
  const b = 2;
  return <div>{a}{b}</div>;
}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### an arrow component named by its variable

```toml
[rules."react/component-max-lines".options]
max = 3
```

```jsx
const Card = () => {
  const a = 1;
  const b = 2;
  return <div>{a}{b}</div>;
};
```

**Reports** at `1:7`.

#### memo and forwardRef wrap a component

```toml
[rules."react/component-max-lines".options]
max = 3
```

```jsx
const Card = memo(
  forwardRef((props, ref) => {
    const a = 1;
    return <div ref={ref}>{a}</div>;
  }),
);
```

**Reports** at `1:7`.

#### a class component

```toml
[rules."react/component-max-lines".options]
max = 3
```

```jsx
class Card extends React.Component {
  render() {
    const a = 1;
    return <div>{a}</div>;
  }
}
```

**Reports** at `1:7`.

#### a lower-case function that returns JSX is not a component

```toml
[rules."react/component-max-lines".options]
max = 3
```

```jsx
function renderCard() {
  const a = 1;
  const b = 2;
  return <div>{a}{b}</div>;
}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### blank lines and comments are not counted

```toml
[rules."react/component-max-lines".options]
max = 4
```

```jsx
function Card() {
  // note

  const a = 1;
  return <div>{a}</div>;
}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### ignore_names exempts a component

```toml
[rules."react/component-max-lines".options]
max = 3
ignore_names = "^Card"
```

```jsx
function Card() {
  const a = 1;
  const b = 2;
  return <div>{a}{b}</div>;
}
```

**Reports nothing.**

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "react/component-max-lines" = { options = { max = 3 } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "react/component-max-lines" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"react/component-max-lines" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"react/component-max-lines" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"react/component-max-lines" = { severity = "warn", options = { max = 3 } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "react/component-max-lines": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"max": 3}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JSX:** `// codelaw-ignore react/component-max-lines: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore react/component-max-lines expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule react/component-max-lines --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain react/component-max-lines       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule react/component-max-lines  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>             # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Find a block of markup with its own name (a row, a header, a modal) and move it into a component of its own, passing in what it reads as props.
2. Move state and effects that belong to one part into a custom hook (`useTableSort`).
3. If the component is long on purpose, name it in `ignore_names`, or freeze it with `codelaw baseline add --rule react/component-max-lines`.

## Examples

### JSX

#### Don't

*With these options:* `{ max = 4 }`

```jsx
function Card({ title, body }) {
  const heading = <h2>{title}</h2>;
  const text = <p>{body}</p>;
  const footer = <small>end</small>;
  return <div>{heading}{text}{footer}</div>;
}
```

#### Do

*With these options:* `{ max = 4 }`

```jsx
function Card({ title, body }) {
  return <div><h2>{title}</h2><p>{body}</p></div>;
}
```

### TSX

#### Don't

*With these options:* `{ max = 4 }`

```tsx
function Card({ title, body }: CardProps) {
  const heading = <h2>{title}</h2>;
  const text = <p>{body}</p>;
  const footer = <small>end</small>;
  return <div>{heading}{text}{footer}</div>;
}
```

#### Do

*With these options:* `{ max = 4 }`

```tsx
function Card({ title, body }: CardProps) {
  return <div><h2>{title}</h2><p>{body}</p></div>;
}
```
